\]

\]

Orthogonal matrices preserve norms:

\[
\|Ax\|=\|x\|
\]

\[
Av=\lambda v
\]

Taking norms,

\[
\|Av\|=\|\lambda v\|=|\lambda|\|v\|
\]

But \(\|Av\|=\|v\|\), so

\[
|\lambda|\|v\|=\|v\|
\]

Since \(v\neq 0\),

\[
|\lambda|=1
\]

Hence, **(B) is correct**.

**(C)**  
The norm preservation part is true:

\[
\|Ax\|=\|x\|
\]

But orthogonal matrices also preserve inner products:

\[
(Ax)^T(Ay)=x^T A^T A y=x^T y
\]

So the statement saying

\[
(Ax)^T(Ay)\neq x^T y
\]

is false.

Hence, **(C) is incorrect**.

**(D)**  
As shown above,

\[
\|Ax\|=\|x\|
\]

and

\[
(Ax)^T(Ay)=x^T y
\]

for all \(x,y\in \mathbb{R}^n\).

Hence, **(D) is correct**.
